report:
The group reached agreement on a plan, with one step still in progress.

The agreed plan: a technician inspects and repairs the leaking espresso machine, B gives 10 to 15 minutes for the discussion, A and C take on no repair, cleaning, or follow-up duties, and a review date is set in advance. If the machine keeps breaking down, the group will revisit a simpler machine and keep the old one as a keepsake for B, since it belonged to B's late father. The grinder is working and needs no action.

Agreed points from each person: C wants the setup working again but will not coordinate the repair and leans toward the repair option if the budget holder approves and no duties fall to C. A prefers a simpler machine with little upkeep and agrees to the repair option only if the repair and follow-up sit with someone else and a review date is agreed in advance. B wants the old machine repaired and kept, agrees to the repair option if the budget holder approves, and suggested the office manager or purchasing may know who owns the machine.

Open step: nobody knows who owns the machine or who approves the repair cost, and I cannot move money or make that decision. B has agreed to send one short message to the office manager or purchasing asking who owns it and who approves the cost, but has not sent it yet. No review date has been agreed.

I kept one numbered list throughout, in the order concerns were raised, and showed it to all three people each time it changed. It now has 11 entries.
